newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Dragon Oil sees production pick-up in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Dragon Oil sees production pick-up in 1997.

text.p: Irish-based oil and exploration company Dragon Oil Plc said on Thursday said it expected oil production to "increase substantially" in its Caspian Sea well in 1997.
The company said it had completed a successful hot oil drilling operation in the Block II well in the Caspian Sea, offshore Turkmenistan, and that work was contining on schedule.

"Seismic data is being analysed and a new drilling programme will begin in the first quarter of 1997. As a result production is expected to increase substantially throughout 1997," Dragon said in a half-year results statement.

The company noted that average production for the first six months of 1996 in the Block II well was 620 barrels of oil equivalent per day (bpoed) and that it was currently over 1,800 boepd, with more oil being drilled from the company's Caspian Sea operations.
Dragon reduced its net loss to US$0.2 million for the first half of 1996 from US$1.2 million in the same period in 1995.

Dragon said book net assets attributable to shareholders had doubled to over US$135 at the end of June compared with the end of 1995 and that net current assets increased to US$53 million from US$16 million.
The company also said it achieved success on a Gulf of Mexico well and that drilling was beginning soon off the coast of Thailand.
